title: This Bird Eats Its Own Feathers, Then Feeds Them to Its Chicks
subject: grebe

scenes.text: This bird eats its own feathers. Then it feeds them to its chicks.
Grebes swallow feathers on purpose. An eared grebe can cough up as many as six feather balls in one evening.
Chicks get them too. Parents feed feathers to newly hatched chicks.
Why? Grebes eat fish and insects with sharp bones and hard shells that can hurt a stomach.
The leading idea: the feathers form a mat that shields the stomach lining and slows digestion.
Later the bird coughs up the bones in a tidy ball, like an owl pellet. Feathers as armor.

description:
Grebes eat their own feathers, and they feed them to their chicks too.
The leading explanation is that the feathers form a mat in the stomach that protects it from sharp fish bones and hard insect shells, then wrap the leftovers into a ball the bird coughs up, like an owl pellet.
Would you eat armor for dinner?
first_comment: Grebes also carry their chicks on their backs. Which weird bird habit should we do next?
